![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14268429/assets/2f11d5b11c53f7b826291e0b7e95828f57d6f1242b768baf12c874be229b2935.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3x}{5}+C),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
questions.worked_solution:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3x}{5}+C) \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3}{5}(x+\frac{5C}{3}))\end{aligned}
$$

The factor $x+\frac{5C}{3}$ indicates that the graph of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3}{5}(x+\frac{5C}{3}))$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3x}{5}).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14268429/assets/5e9b6568ec493d95db6fe72a6a19024326c5b920629e9ff44a85db54089aa2a6.png)

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3x}{5})$ by $\frac{\pi }{3}-0=\frac{\pi }{3}$ units to the right. Therefore:

$$
\frac{5C}{3}=-\frac{\pi }{3}\,⟹\,C=(-\frac{\pi }{3})(\frac{3}{5})\,⟹\,C=-\frac{\pi }{5}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $-\frac{\pi }{5}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $-\frac{\pi }{5}.$

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3x}{2}+C),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
questions.worked_solution:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3x}{2}+C) \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3}{2}(x+\frac{2C}{3}))\end{aligned}
$$

The factor $x+\frac{2C}{3}$ indicates that the graph of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3}{2}(x+\frac{2C}{3}))$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3x}{2}).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14268429/assets/6438f318c33223abe9f3d2102e6f9f35bf2a8a6e887955ec9230d22e8294536a.png)

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3x}{2})$ by $\frac{\pi }{4}-0=\frac{\pi }{4}$ units to the right. Therefore

$$
\frac{2C}{3}=-\frac{\pi }{4}\,⟹\,C=-\frac{3\pi }{8}.
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $-\frac{3\pi }{8}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $-\frac{3\pi }{8}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14268429/assets/a40509b3b31acce76da67837e9605ba4efd0d588feab227d9354bc5bab0582af.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx)+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B-2D?$
questions.worked_solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{5}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\frac{\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{B}\,⟹\,B=\frac{\pi }{(\frac{\pi }{5})}=5.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the cotangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $-\frac{3}{2}$ unit down. Hence, $D=-\frac{3}{2}.$

Therefore, $B-2D=5-2\cdot (-\frac{3}{2})=5+3=8.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(5x)-\frac{3}{2}.
$$
